heuristics.rule: CGRS-D applicants must not exceed 36 months of full-time doctoral study by December 31 of the application year
heuristics.condition: When a doctoral student is applying for CGRS-D funding
heuristics.action: Submit application before completing 36 months of full-time doctoral enrollment counted to December 31 of the application year
heuristics.because: Exceeding 36 months of doctoral study disqualifies the applicant from CGRS-D eligibility
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: Vanier eligibility window closes at 20 months of full-time doctoral study as of May 1 of the application year
heuristics.condition: When a doctoral student is being considered for Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship nomination
heuristics.action: Ensure candidate has completed no more than 20 months of full-time doctoral study as of May 1 of the application year
heuristics.because: Exceeding 20 months disqualifies the candidate from Vanier eligibility, which has a narrower window than CGRS-D
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: A person may submit a maximum of three lifetime applications for CGRS-D
heuristics.condition: When a doctoral student is planning to apply for CGRS-D
heuristics.action: Track total number of CGRS-D applications submitted across all attempts; do not exceed three
heuristics.because: The three-application lifetime cap is a hard eligibility limit; exceeding it bars further applications
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D applicants who have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC are ineligible
heuristics.condition: When a student previously received a doctoral-level award from any of the three Tri-Council agencies
heuristics.action: Do not apply for CGRS-D; eligibility is forfeited
heuristics.because: Prior receipt of any Tri-Council doctoral scholarship is an explicit disqualifying condition for CGRS-D
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: Vanier nominees cannot have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC
heuristics.condition: When a department is selecting candidates for Vanier nomination
heuristics.action: Confirm candidate has not previously received a doctoral-level Tri-Council scholarship before nominating
heuristics.because: Prior receipt of a Tri-Council doctoral award is an explicit disqualifying condition for Vanier
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: International students may receive up to 15% of available CGRS-D awards
heuristics.condition: When an international student applies for CGRS-D at a Canadian institution
heuristics.action: Verify with the administering agency whether international students are included in the allocation for the relevant discipline
heuristics.because: International students compete within a capped 15% allocation, significantly reducing available awards compared to domestic students
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D applicants must apply to the single agency matching their primary research discipline
heuristics.condition: When a student is in an interdisciplinary field and determining which Tri-Council agency to apply to
heuristics.action: Submit to one agency only, selected based on primary discipline; NSERC for natural sciences/engineering, SSHRC for social sciences/humanities/arts, CIHR for health research
heuristics.because: Each applicant submits to only one agency; submitting to multiple agencies is not permitted
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — agency assignment rules

heuristics.rule: Direct agency CGRS-D submissions are due October 17 at 8:00 PM ET
heuristics.condition: When a student is submitting a CGRS-D application directly to the agency rather than through their institution
heuristics.action: Submit through ResearchNet by October 17 at 8:00 PM ET
heuristics.because: The direct agency deadline is a fixed hard deadline; late submissions are not accepted
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — application deadlines

heuristics.rule: Vanier students cannot apply directly; nominations must be submitted by the institution
heuristics.condition: When a student wishes to be considered for a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship
heuristics.action: Request consideration from the department/institution, which must nominate the candidate on the student's behalf
heuristics.because: Direct student applications are not accepted; the institution controls nomination eligibility and submission
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program documentation — process

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D selection criteria are weighted equally: 50% Research Potential, 50% Experience & Achievements
heuristics.condition: When a student is preparing a CGRS-D application
heuristics.action: Allocate equal preparation effort to the research proposal (quality, methodology, significance, originality, ethical conduct, communication) and to documenting achievements (academic record, scholarships, teaching/mentoring, project management, community engagement)
heuristics.because: Both criteria carry equal formal weight in adjudication; neglecting either half disadvantages the application
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — selection criteria

heuristics.rule: Up to 10 additional CGRS-D awards are reserved for self-identified Black student researchers
heuristics.condition: When a self-identified Black student researcher is applying for CGRS-D
heuristics.action: Self-identify as a Black student researcher in the application to be considered for the reserved allocation
heuristics.because: A dedicated pool of up to 10 additional awards exists specifically for this group, separate from the general competition
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — special provisions

heuristics.rule: Indigenous CGRS-D applicants may receive consideration beyond institutional quotas
heuristics.condition: When an Indigenous applicant is applying for CGRS-D through an institution with a quota
heuristics.action: Note Indigenous status in the application; the application may be considered outside standard institutional quota limits
heuristics.because: Official policy explicitly provides for consideration beyond institutional quotas for Indigenous applicants
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — special provisions

heuristics.rule: The 2024 budget stipend increases apply only to Tri-Council grant recipients, not to students funded through supervisor research grants
heuristics.condition: When assessing whether a PhD student will benefit from the 2024 federal budget increase to graduate stipends
heuristics.action: Confirm whether the student holds a Tri-Council award; students funded solely through supervisor grants are excluded from the increase
heuristics.because: The CAD $825 million allocation over five years explicitly excludes graduate students funded through supervisor research grants
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Canada 2024 Federal Budget — graduate funding provisions; Chemistry World 2024 reporting

decision_factors.factor: Months of full-time doctoral study completed at time of application
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines eligibility for CGRS-D (cap: 36 months by December 31) and Vanier (cap: 20 months as of May 1); exceeding the threshold results in disqualification
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count full-time doctoral enrollment months from program start date to the relevant deadline date specified for each award

decision_factors.factor: Prior receipt of Tri-Council doctoral scholarship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Disqualifies applicant from both CGRS-D and Vanier; a hard ineligibility condition with no exceptions stated
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether candidate has ever received a doctoral-level award from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC

decision_factors.factor: Canadian citizenship, permanent residency, or protected person status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Domestic applicants compete in the main pool; international students are limited to 15% of available CGRS-D awards, significantly reducing odds
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify immigration status at time of application; international students must also confirm enrollment at a Canadian institution

decision_factors.factor: Research discipline alignment with administering Tri-Council agency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines which agency administers the application; submitting to the wrong agency or to multiple agencies is not permitted
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Match primary research discipline to agency: NSERC (natural sciences, engineering, math, CS), SSHRC (social sciences, humanities, arts), CIHR (health sciences, biomedical research); for interdisciplinary work, select by primary discipline

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Vanier nominations are institution-controlled and limited in number; a student cannot self-nominate regardless of qualification
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Inquire directly with department about whether it nominates Vanier candidates and the number of nominations available to the institution

decision_factors.factor: Research Potential — proposal quality, methodology, significance, originality, critical thinking, ethical conduct, communication
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Constitutes 50% of CGRS-D selection score; directly affects award outcome
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluated by adjudication committee against stated sub-criteria: proposal quality, methodology, significance, originality, critical thinking, ethical conduct, communication

decision_factors.factor: Experience and Achievements — academic record, scholarships, teaching/mentoring, project management, community engagement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Constitutes 50% of CGRS-D selection score; directly affects award outcome
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluated by adjudication committee against stated sub-criteria: academic record, prior scholarships received, teaching/mentoring, project management, community engagement

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students are limited to three lifetime applications; exceeding this forfeits eligibility permanently
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count all previous CGRS-D (and formerly CGS-D/PGS-D/SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship) applications submitted across all institutions

decision_factors.why_it_matters: One of three equally weighted Vanier selection criteria; absence of demonstrated leadership disqualifies candidates in committee review
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assessed equally alongside academic excellence and research potential; must be demonstrated not inferred

decision_factors.factor: Whether student holds a Tri-Council award (for 2024 budget stipend increase)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Only Tri-Council award holders benefit from the 2024 federal budget stipend increases; supervisor-grant-funded students are excluded
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether student holds CGRS-D, Vanier, CGS-M, or other Tri-Council award at time of stipend disbursement

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Starting a PhD program and delaying CGRS-D application until second or third year
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The 36-month eligibility window is counted to December 31 of the application year; delaying the first application consumes the eligibility window and may leave fewer remaining lifetime applications before the window closes
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PhD students who are unaware of the interaction between the 36-month cap and the three-application lifetime limit

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on supervisor research grant funding rather than pursuing Tri-Council awards
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The 2024 federal budget stipend increases (PhD: CAD $40,000/year; postdoc: CAD $70,000/year) explicitly exclude students funded through supervisor research grants; only Tri-Council award holders receive the increase
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: The majority of graduate students, who are funded through supervisor grants rather than direct Tri-Council awards, per the source text

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Applying for CGRS-D as an international student
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: International students compete within a capped 15% allocation of available awards, meaning their effective odds are significantly lower than domestic applicants even with identical qualifications
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International doctoral students at Canadian institutions who assume they compete in the same pool as domestic students

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Assuming CGRS-D and CGS-D/PGS-D/SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship are separate programs with separate lifetime limits
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The formerly separate programs (CGS-D, PGS-D, SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship) have been merged into CGRS-D; prior applications under the old names likely count toward the three-application lifetime limit
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Returning or continuing doctoral students who applied under predecessor program names and do not realize those applications may count against their lifetime limit

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Pursuing Vanier without confirming institutional nomination capacity
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Students cannot apply directly to Vanier; if the institution does not nominate the student, the award is inaccessible regardless of the student's qualifications
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Highly competitive international and domestic students who meet all academic criteria but attend institutions with limited or no nomination slots

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Applying for CGRS-D through an institution with a quota rather than directly to the agency
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Institutional quotas may limit the number of applications the institution forwards to the agency; direct agency submission may be an alternative route but has its own fixed deadline (October 17, 8:00 PM ET)
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students at institutions with tight internal quotas who assume their application will automatically be forwarded

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying for CGRS-D after exceeding 36 months of full-time doctoral study by December 31 of the application year
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The 36-month doctoral study cap is a hard eligibility cutoff enforced at the application review stage
failure_patterns.consequence: Application is deemed ineligible and rejected
warning_signs: Student is in third year of doctoral studies and has not yet applied
Student loses track of enrollment months due to leaves of absence or part-time transitions

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying for CGRS-D or Vanier after having previously received a doctoral-level Tri-Council scholarship
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Prior receipt of any doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC is an explicit disqualifying condition for both awards
failure_patterns.consequence: Application is deemed ineligible and rejected
warning_signs: Student previously held CGS-D, PGS-D, or SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship under the predecessor programs
Student received a CIHR doctoral award and then switches disciplines to apply to NSERC

failure_patterns.pattern: Submitting a fourth CGRS-D application after having already made three lifetime applications
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The three-application lifetime cap is a hard eligibility rule; no exceptions are stated in the program documentation
warning_signs: Student has applied in multiple years without success and attempts a fourth application
Student does not track applications made under predecessor program names

failure_patterns.pattern: International student applies for CGRS-D expecting to compete in the full award pool
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: International students are capped at 15% of available awards; competition is within a restricted allocation
failure_patterns.consequence: Significantly reduced probability of award; application may be ineligible if the 15% allocation for the discipline is exhausted
warning_signs: International student assumes equal competition with domestic applicants
Student does not verify whether their discipline's agency includes international students in the 15% allocation

failure_patterns.pattern: Student attempts to self-apply for Vanier instead of seeking institutional nomination
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Vanier does not accept direct student applications; the institution must nominate the candidate
failure_patterns.consequence: Application cannot be submitted; student is excluded from consideration for that cycle
warning_signs: Student attempts to access Vanier application portal independently
Student does not consult department about nomination process before the institutional nomination deadline

failure_patterns.pattern: Interdisciplinary student submits CGRS-D applications to multiple Tri-Council agencies in the same cycle
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Program rules require submission to a single agency based on primary discipline; multiple submissions are not permitted
warning_signs: Student with health-engineering interdisciplinary research attempts to apply to both NSERC and CIHR
Student is uncertain about primary discipline and hedges by applying to more than one agency

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant completed more than 36 months of full-time doctoral study by December 31 of the application year?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the doctoral study duration eligibility cap for CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for CGRS-D; no further assessment needed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant passes this eligibility threshold; proceed to other criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the prior award disqualification condition applicable to both CGRS-D and Vanier
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for both CGRS-D and Vanier
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant passes this eligibility threshold; proceed to other criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant previously submitted three or more CGRS-D (or predecessor CGS-D/PGS-D/SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship) applications?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the three-application lifetime limit for CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant has exhausted lifetime eligibility for CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant has remaining lifetime applications; proceed to evaluate application content

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person, or an international student?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the applicant competes in the main pool or within the 15% international student allocation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Domestic applicant competes in main pool
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: International applicant is limited to 15% allocation; verify whether the relevant agency includes international students in that allocation

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the applicant's primary research discipline — natural sciences/engineering, social sciences/humanities/arts, or health sciences?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines which Tri-Council agency (NSERC, SSHRC, or CIHR) administers the application
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Match to appropriate agency and confirm single-agency submission
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: For interdisciplinary applicants, require selection of primary discipline before submission

diagnostic_questions.question: For Vanier: Has the applicant completed more than 20 months of full-time doctoral study as of May 1 of the application year?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the doctoral study duration eligibility cap specific to Vanier, which is narrower than CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for Vanier; may still be eligible for CGRS-D if within 36-month window
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant passes Vanier eligibility threshold; confirm institution is willing and able to nominate

diagnostic_questions.question: For Vanier: Does the applicant's institution have available nomination slots, and has the department confirmed willingness to nominate the candidate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests whether the institutional nomination gate is accessible to the student
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate may proceed with nomination process through institution
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate cannot access Vanier regardless of academic qualifications; no alternative self-application route exists

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the applicant hold a Tri-Council award (CGRS-D, Vanier, CGS-M, or equivalent)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the applicant benefits from the 2024 federal budget stipend increases
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is eligible for new stipend levels (PhD: CAD $40,000/year; postdoc: CAD $70,000/year)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant funded through supervisor grants is excluded from the 2024 budget increase

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the applicant self-identify as a Black student researcher?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines eligibility for the reserved pool of up to 10 additional CGRS-D awards for Black student researchers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant should self-identify in the application to be considered for the dedicated award pool
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant competes in the general pool; no access to the reserved 10 awards

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant Indigenous?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the applicant may receive consideration beyond standard institutional quotas under CGRS-D special provisions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may be considered outside institutional quota limits; confirm this provision applies to the relevant agency stream
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant subject to standard institutional quota rules

industry_realities.common_belief: The 2024 federal budget increase to graduate student stipends benefits all Canadian PhD students
industry_realities.actual_reality: The CAD $825 million increase exclusively benefits Tri-Council award holders; the majority of graduate students funded through supervisor research grants are explicitly excluded
industry_realities.implication: Students and advisors should not assume PhD offers will automatically reflect the new stipend targets unless the student holds or will hold a Tri-Council award

industry_realities.common_belief: CGS-D, PGS-D, and SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship are separate programs with separate application histories
industry_realities.actual_reality: All three have been merged into the unified CGRS-D program; they are no longer distinct programs
industry_realities.implication: Students who previously applied under the old program names should treat those applications as part of their CGRS-D history, particularly regarding the three-application lifetime limit

industry_realities.common_belief: Any qualified student can apply directly to Vanier
industry_realities.actual_reality: Students cannot apply directly to Vanier; the institution must nominate the candidate, and the number of nominations per institution is limited
industry_realities.implication: Qualifying for Vanier requires both meeting eligibility criteria and securing an institutional nomination, which is a separate gatekeeping step entirely outside the student's direct control

industry_realities.common_belief: International students compete equally with domestic students for CGRS-D awards
industry_realities.actual_reality: International students are allocated up to 15% of available CGRS-D awards, a formally capped and separate allocation from the main pool
industry_realities.implication: International students face structurally lower odds of receiving CGRS-D regardless of application quality; funding strategy for international PhD students in Canada must account for this limitation

industry_realities.common_belief: CGRS-D and Vanier have the same eligibility window for doctoral study duration
industry_realities.actual_reality: CGRS-D allows up to 36 months of doctoral study by December 31; Vanier requires no more than 20 months as of May 1 — a significantly narrower window measured to an earlier date
industry_realities.implication: Students competitive enough for Vanier must be nominated earlier in their doctoral program; missing the 20-month window eliminates Vanier eligibility even if the student remains eligible for CGRS-D

industry_realities.common_belief: A student can apply to multiple Tri-Council agencies if their research is interdisciplinary
industry_realities.actual_reality: Applicants must submit to a single agency based on their primary research discipline; multiple submissions are not permitted
industry_realities.implication: Interdisciplinary students must make a deliberate, binding determination of primary discipline before submitting and cannot hedge across agencies

industry_realities.common_belief: Tri-Council doctoral awards represent the standard funding level for Canadian PhD students
industry_realities.actual_reality: Per Professor Bruce Arndtsen (McGill), many departments had to top up these fellowships from research grants simply to reach their normal stipend level, suggesting Tri-Council award values have historically been below institutional norms in some fields
industry_realities.implication: Prospective students should not treat the CGRS-D CAD $40,000/year value as automatically sufficient or above-market for their discipline and institution

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding the eligibility window for CGRS-D vs. Vanier
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes both awards have the same application window; plans to apply 'in the first few years' without tracking exact months
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Tracks months of full-time doctoral enrollment precisely; knows CGRS-D closes at 36 months to December 31 and Vanier closes at 20 months to May 1, and plans application cycles accordingly from day one of enrollment
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Missing the Vanier window by even one month forfeits the most prestigious Canadian doctoral scholarship permanently; missing CGRS-D window forfeits up to CAD $120,000

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Approach to the 2024 budget stipend increase
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes PhD offers will automatically reflect the new CAD $40,000/year target after the 2024 budget announcement
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows the increase applies only to Tri-Council award holders; explicitly asks departments what percentage of students receive Tri-Council funding and what non-award students are paid
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Most PhD students are funded through supervisor grants and will not see the increase; salary negotiation and program comparison must be based on actual offer terms, not budget announcements

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Researches Vanier eligibility criteria and assumes the path is to build a strong application and submit it
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows students cannot self-apply; proactively asks the department whether it nominates Vanier candidates and whether the student would be considered, before or at admission — understanding that institutional gate-keeping is the binding constraint
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A student who does not secure a nomination cannot access Vanier regardless of qualifications; the nomination process must be initiated by the student asking the institution, not by submitting an application

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Applies to both NSERC and CIHR (or SSHRC and CIHR) for an interdisciplinary project, believing multiple submissions increase chances
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows only a single agency submission is permitted; deliberately identifies and commits to primary discipline for agency selection before the application cycle opens
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Multiple submissions are not permitted; submitting to the wrong or multiple agencies risks disqualification and wastes a lifetime application

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Impact of prior Tri-Council awards on future eligibility
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Views receiving a CGS-M or other Master's-level Tri-Council award as purely positive without considering downstream doctoral eligibility effects
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows that prior receipt of a doctoral-level (not Master's-level) Tri-Council scholarship disqualifies future CGRS-D and Vanier applications; tracks award history carefully to confirm no doctoral-level award has been received
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Receiving a doctoral-level Tri-Council award forfeits all future CGRS-D and Vanier eligibility permanently; students must understand which award tier triggers disqualification

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: International student views CGRS-D as a standard open competition and benchmarks odds against overall acceptance rates
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows international students compete within a formally capped 15% allocation; adjusts award probability estimates accordingly and verifies whether the relevant agency includes international students in that allocation for the specific discipline
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Overestimating CGRS-D odds leads to insufficient backup funding planning; international students need alternative funding strategies that account for the structural 15% cap
